verdict.reasoning: Patient describes chest discomfort in the middle of the chest, pressure-like, lasting a couple of hours: 'it's been ongoing for, a couple of hours now... it's somewhere in the middle of my chest... it feels like it's pressure.'
Patient explicitly describes the sensation: 'If I had to describe what discomfort feeling, it's, it's like someone's sitting on my chest.'

Radiation pattern is described: head denied, left shoulder/arm affirmed, no further spread: 'Have you noticed this pressure, radiating to your head?' 'not to my head, no.' 'how about to your left, or right arm?' 'Yes. There is some pain in my left shoulder and arm.' 'does that pain go anywhere else? ... or to your back?' 'no.'
Associated symptoms stated: 'I've got shortness of breath. And I feel slightly, light-headed.' and later 'I've noticed nausea, but no vomiting, yet.'

No dysphagia and normal bowel/urinary habits are documented: 'have you noticed any problems swallowing, or drinking water?' 'no.' and 'have you noticed any problems going to the loo?' 'no problems going to the loo.'

Exertional dyspnea without chest pain is described: 'I've had, some difficulty climbing the stairs. And, if I have to sort of walk uphill, there's that sort of challenge as well.' and to pain: 'when you get short of breath, when you're walking up the stairs, have you noticed any pain?' 'Um, no pain as such, but there's often calf pain and, leg swellings.' (no chest pain reported).
Patient reports both calf pain and leg swelling: 'there's often calf pain and, leg swellings.'
Past medical history given: 'high cholesterol, and, I've had hypertension, hypertension.' Doctor confirms: 'that's high blood pressure, and high cholesterol.'
Medication use is denied: 'Do you take any medicines for that?' ... 'No, I don't take any medicine.'
Smoking and living situation documented: patient answers 'Uh, yes I do smoke, yeah.' and later 'do you live at home with your wife at the moment?' 'yes.'

Gardening frequency and activity limitation are both described: 'how often do you do gardening?' 'every other week. So, fortnightly.' and 'there's some problems just, performing daily activities... I try to limit my daily activity to just moving around the house, nothing too strenuous.'

Symptoms and suspected cardiac cause are all in the transcript: chest pressure with left arm radiation and SOB, light-headedness, nausea are described as above; doctor states concern for cardiac etiology: 'my concern is, it might be something to do with your heart.' and 'I'm always worried about the heart first, before anything else.'
Pulmonary causes are explicitly mentioned: 'there are two things they will be worried about. The one is your chest, so, your heart. And the second is your breathing, which is your lungs.'

Dyspnea on exertion with calf pain and leg swelling is described: exertional SOB on stairs/uphill is noted, and in same context: 'when you get short of breath... have you noticed any pain?' 'no pain as such, but there's often calf pain and, leg swellings.'
Urgent ambulance/hospital evaluation arranged: 'I think it might be worth, you calling an ambulance... get you to the hospital as soon as possible... While to you, I will ring an ambulance.'

Instructions to stay on phone, rest, keep calm, drink water: 'in the meantime, I think we should stay on the phone...' and later 'The ambulance should be there very soon. In the meantime, I would suggest that you stay calm, and have some water if you need to.'
Doctor advises against taking medications: 'Don't take any of those medications.'

Planned EMS actions and ED consultant review are stated: 'they will give you lots of things to breathe through, and attach things to your arms. Just to check, things like your blood pressure, and your heart rate.' and 'When you get to the hospital, you'll be seen by a consultant, pretty, pretty much immediately.'

While dyspnea on exertion and leg swelling are discussed as history, there is no explicit statement that ED workup will specifically evaluate these issues; the note infers a workup focus not directly stated.
Follow-up after hospital visit is planned: 'I'll um, book another appointment, to see you soon. Uh, , once you've had your adventure.' indicating follow-up after hospital care.
